overall: Tomorrow (Monday, June 22) in Atlanta is expected to be partly sunny with a 30% chance of afternoon showers and thunderstorms developing after 11am, driven by a southwest flow and modest moisture. The NWS official forecast targets a high near 89°F, similar to today's observed 87.8°F. The active flood advisory affects only southwest Georgia counties and expires tonight, posing no direct impact on the Atlanta metro area.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable model divergence: HRRR (~87.7°F) and NBM (~88.6°F) cluster in the warm upper-80s range consistent with the NWS official forecast, while GFS (~82.2°F) and ECMWF (~83.7°F) run 5-6°F cooler, likely reflecting stronger precipitation-induced cooling scenarios. max_temp_prediction: The odd-bucket Tier 1 signal (89-90°F at 27.0%, gap of 22.7 points) is the strongest directional indicator and aligns tightly with the NWS official high of ~89°F and the forecast-only model at 88.9°F. The primary downside risk is the cooler GFS/ECMWF scenario where early cloud cover or convection limits the peak; confidence is moderate-to-high in the 87-90°F range with 89°F as the best single estimate.
